title: RNOR Status: Saving Tax on Foreign Income for Returning NRIs
description: Returning Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can qualify for Resident Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) status for a few years. RNOR status offers a significant tax adv.

faq.q: What are the key conditions to qualify as an RNOR?
faq.a: You qualify as an RNOR if you are a Resident in the current financial year but have been a Non-Resident in India for 9 out of the 10 preceding financial years, OR have been in India for 729 days or less during the 7 preceding financial years.

faq.q: How long can an individual typically remain an RNOR?
faq.a: For most returning NRIs, the RNOR status can last for up to two financial years, depending on their exact dates of arrival and prior stay history in India.

faq.q: Is all foreign income exempt for an RNOR?
faq.a: Generally, yes, unless the foreign income is derived from a business controlled in or a profession set up in India. For example, rental income from an overseas property or interest from a foreign bank account is usually exempt.

faq.q: Do I need to declare my foreign assets and income in my Indian ITR as an RNOR?
faq.a: While foreign income may not be taxable for an RNOR, you are still required to report your residential status and may need to disclose certain foreign assets in your ITR, depending on the specific forms and rules applicable. It's best to consult a tax expert.

faq.q: Can I repatriate funds from my NRE account during my RNOR period?
faq.a: Yes, funds from NRE accounts are fully repatriable. The principal and interest earned on NRE accounts are tax-exempt in India for all residential statuses, including RNOR and ROR.

faq.q: What happens to my foreign income once I become an ROR?
faq.a: Once you become a Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR), your worldwide income, including all foreign income, becomes taxable in India. Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) may offer relief, but the income must be declared.

faq.q: Should I sell my foreign investments before returning to India?
faq.a: It depends on your specific situation. Selling foreign investments while still an NRI or during your RNOR period can help you avoid Indian capital gains tax on those transactions. However, consider the tax implications in the country where the assets are located and consult a financial advisor.
